items.text: Topos theory — 1
Four sessions on topoi — « essentially on general topology ».
A topos: the main object of study of topology; topoi generalise classical general topology.
Prerequisites: topological spaces and continuous maps; the language of categories.
§ Review of sheaves on a topological space
Let $X$ be a topological space,
\mathcal O = \mathcal O(X) = \{\text{open subsets of } X\}
stable under arbitrary unions and finite intersections; ordered by inclusion.
An ordered set is a category (denoted $\mathcal O$ again):
\operatorname{Hom}(U,V)=\begin{cases}\varnothing & U\not\subset V\\ \{U\hookrightarrow V\} & U\subset V\end{cases}
Arrows: the graph of the order relation.
Presheaves
A presheaf (of sets) on $X$: a contravariant functor
F\colon \mathcal O^{\circ} \longrightarrow \mathbf{Sets}
U \mapsto F(U), \qquad U\subset V \;\mapsto\; \rho_{UV}\colon F(V)\to F(U) \quad\text{(restriction)}
U\subset V\subset W:\ \rho_{UW}=\rho_{UV}\circ\rho_{VW},\qquad \rho_{UU}=\mathrm{id}_{F(U)}
\{\text{presheaves on } X\} = \operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O^{\circ},\mathbf{Sets})\quad\text{(a category of functors)}
A morphism $f\colon F\to G$: maps $f(U)\colon F(U)\to G(U)$ such that, for $U\subset V$,
\begin{CD} F(V) @>{f(V)}>> G(V)\\ @V{\rho}VV @VV{\rho}V\\ F(U) @>{f(U)}>> G(U) \end{CD}
commutes. Composition with $g\colon G\to H$: $(g\circ f)(U) = g(U)\circ f(U)$.
Sheaves
So far only the order on $\mathcal O$ was used; now its being the open sets of $X$.
$F$ is separated if for every open $U$ and every covering $U=\bigcup_i U_i$ (i.e. $U=\sup_i U_i$ in $\mathcal O$),
F(U)\longrightarrow \prod_i F(U_i)\quad\text{is injective.}
Elements of $F(U)$: sections of $F$ over $U$.
$\rho_{UV}(f)=f|_U$: the restriction of the section $f$ to $U$. Separated: a section is known by its restrictions $f|_{U_i}$.
A family $(f_i)$, $f_i\in F(U_i)$, coming from a section $f\in F(U)$ satisfies the necessary condition
f_i|_{U_i\cap U_j} = f_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}\qquad\forall\, i,j
$F$ is a sheaf if moreover $F(U)$ is identified with the set of families satisfying it:
F(U)\longrightarrow \prod_{i\in I}F(U_i)\;\rightrightarrows\;\prod_{(i,j)\in I\times I}F(U_i\cap U_j)\quad\text{exact}
« Exact »: the first arrow identifies $F(U)$ with the kernel of the double arrow, the elements with the same image under both.
Morphisms of sheaves: morphisms of the underlying presheaves.
\operatorname{Top}(X) \subset \operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O^{\circ},\mathbf{Sets})\quad\text{full subcategory: the sheaves on } X
Examples
1. $E$ a set; $F(U)=E^U$, the maps $U\to E$; restriction of maps.
A sheaf (true even for non-open sets): the sheaf of maps from $X$ into $E$.
Subpresheaves. $G\subset F$ if $G(U)\subset F(U)$ for all $U$, with the restrictions induced by those of $F$.
A subfunctor; that is, subsets $G(U)\subset F(U)$ stable under restriction.
$F$, $G$ sheaves: $G$ a subsheaf of $F$ if a subpresheaf.
If $F$ is separated, a subpresheaf $G$ is separated.
If $F$ is a sheaf, $G$ is a sheaf iff « belonging to $G$ » is a property of local nature:
f\in G(U)\iff f|_{U_i}\in G(U_i)\ \ \forall i
A property of local type of sections = a subsheaf.
2. $E$ a topological space (a set: discrete topology): continuous maps $U\to E$; continuity is local — a subsheaf of 1.
3. $X$, $E$ differentiable varieties ($C^\infty$ or $C^r$): differentiable maps $U\to E$ — a subsheaf of 2.
Likewise analytic varieties, analytic spaces…
4. A fibre space over $X$ (an $X$-space): $f\colon E\to X$ continuous. Sections over $U$:
\Gamma(U,E/X)=\{\,s\colon U\to E \text{ continuous} : f\circ s = (U\hookrightarrow X)\,\}
Being a section is local: the sheaf of sections of $E$, a subsheaf of 2.
Hence the word « sections » for the elements of $F(U)$.
(From the audience.) Example 2 is a case of 4: maps $U\to E$ = sections of $E\times X\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{pr}_2\ }X$.
5. $X$ locally compact: Radon measures on $U$.
$X$ a differentiable variety ($\mathbb R^n$): distributions — « distributions localise ».
6. $U\mapsto$ closed subsets of $U$, restriction $Z\mapsto Z\cap V$; being closed is local.
Likewise all subsets of $U$ (closed ones: a subsheaf); analytic subsets of an analytic space.
Sheaves: a systematic tool to pass from local data to global data.
References: Godement, Topologie algébrique et théorie des faisceaux (Hermann);
Bredon, Sheaf theory (McGraw-Hill) — mainly cohomological.
Here: little or no sheaf cohomology; the purpose is general topology.
Fibre spaces over $X$ and their sheaves of sections
E\ \longmapsto\ \tilde E = \text{sheaf of (continuous) sections of } E \text{ over open sets of } X
Functorial: a morphism $f\colon E\to F$ of fibre spaces (the triangle commutes)
\begin{CD} E @>{f}>> F\\ @VVV @VVV\\ X @= X \end{CD}
\tilde f\colon \tilde E\to\tilde F,\qquad \tilde f(U)\colon s\mapsto f\circ s
\operatorname{Fib}(X)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Top}(X),\qquad E\mapsto \tilde E
Question. Can $E$ be reconstructed from $\tilde E$ — is this functor fully faithful?
No. Take $X=\{e\}$ a point:
\operatorname{Fib}(\mathrm{pt}) \simeq \{\text{topological spaces}\}
\Gamma_U\colon \operatorname{Top}(X)\to\mathbf{Sets},\quad \Gamma_U(F)=F(U);\qquad \Gamma(F)=\Gamma(X,F)=F(X)
\Gamma\colon \operatorname{Top}(\mathrm{pt})\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathbf{Sets}\quad\text{(equivalence)}
So $E\mapsto\tilde E$ becomes $E\mapsto$ the underlying set of $E$: the forgetful functor,
not fully faithful — the topology is lost.
